conviction_note: The company's own numbers point to a beat-and-raise. Its $199M FY guide implies H2 growth of about 19% against H1 +31%, PIF +31.8% and a higher ceding commission. Against that, the only Q3 demand evidence is proxies: a record-quiet hurricane season through September and the two slowest home-sale months of 2026, and the stock already fell about 16% from its post-Q2 high while they played out. The findings net to +0.4. p_up 55 on a 6% abs move gives +0.6; the two measurements agree in sign and are both small.

findings.finding: Neptune's raised FY2026 guide of $199M revenue is conservative against its own run-rate. H1 revenue was $93.7M (+31.2%), so the guide implies H2 of $105.3M, about +19% y/y against H2 2025 ($44.4M Q3 + $43.8M Q4 = $88.2M). At June 30, premium in force was +31.8% ($419M), policies in force +29.0%, written premium +31%, and the 10-Q says commission income also rose on a higher average ceding commission after both large capacity programs renewed on improved terms in Q2, which applies to all of Q3. The Q3 consensus of about $55M (+24%) is below the June 30 book growth. A revenue print near $56.5-57.5M and an FY raise above the $201-203M Street figure is the likely outcome.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beat and raise in Q2 (+7% revenue surprise, guide raised to $199M): the stock gapped about +6.7% ($30.34 to $32.36 open, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/neptune-insurance-nysenp-shares-gap-up-after-better-than-expected-earnings-2026-07-22/) and rose 17% in the week. FY guide event in Feb 2026: +12.74%. A small Q1 revenue beat (+2%) with a guide raise to $195M: -3.17%. Beats with a meaningful raise have been bought; small beats have not.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus sits at +24% y/y for Q3 and only $2-4M above a guide that implies a sharp H2 deceleration the June 30 book does not show. If the market had priced the run-rate, Q3 estimates would sit near $57M+ and the stock would not be 16% below its post-Q2 high.
findings.independence: The 10-Q for the same quarter (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002067129/000162828026049809/np-20260630.htm) attributes the commission growth to the higher ceding commission and reports 92.1% premium retention. Same company, a different document, same period. Neptune has beaten revenue consensus in Q1 (+2%) and Q2 (+7%) (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/NP).

findings.finding: The 2026 Atlantic season had no hurricane at all through late September, the longest hurricane-free start of the satellite era and the quietest season on record by storm energy through late September. Neptune's own 10-Q says Q2/Q3 sales rise because hurricane season drives awareness, and on the Q2 call management named 'residual slowdown from below-average 2025 storm activity' as a headwind. Q3 new business (and fee income, which tracks new business) is therefore likely soft against Q2's record, and management commentary on new-business momentum may disappoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print has turned on storm-driven new business that can be isolated. Q2 2026 printed record new business despite the cited storm headwind and the stock gapped up.
findings.why_not_priced: It is partly priced: the stock fell from $35 after Q2 to about $27.4 on Oct 2 while the quiet season played out, and rebounded only once Isaias formed. What is not priced is the size of the hit to new-business counts, because no company figure has been disclosed since June 30. Q3 2025 was also quiet, so the y/y comp is softer than the headline suggests.
findings.independence: Proxy. The demand link comes from the company's own 10-Q seasonality language (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002067129/000162828026049809/np-20260630.htm) and the Q2 headwind comment (https://www.reinsurancene.ws/neptune-sees-record-figures-in-q226-with-revenue-reaching-55-9m-and-net-income-15-8m/). The quiet season is corroborated by https://www.bostonglobe.com/2026/09/22/metro/record-quiet-2026-atlantic-hurricane-season/.

findings.finding: US existing-home sales in August and September 2026 were the two slowest months of the year (NAR), with September at 3.99M SAAR, -2.2% y/y, and the 30-year mortgage rate at 6.86% against 6.35% a year earlier. Lender-mandated flood purchases come from home sales, and management named the slow real estate market as a Q2 headwind.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 had the same headwind cited and still printed a +7% revenue beat with the stock gapping up.
findings.why_not_priced: Public macro series and largely known. Its size is small because more than 75% of Q2 new business was voluntary rather than bank-mandated (Q2 presentation).
findings.independence: Macro proxy. Management's Q2 comment on the real estate market is in the Q2 release coverage (https://www.reinsurancene.ws/neptune-sees-record-figures-in-q226-with-revenue-reaching-55-9m-and-net-income-15-8m/).

findings.finding: Hurricane Isaias, the first hurricane of 2026, made landfall near Destin, FL as a Category 2 (105 mph) on Oct 9, with flooding across the Florida Panhandle and Alabama. That gives management a storm-salience tailwind to cite for October/Q4 new business on the Oct 20 call and supports holding or raising the Q4-implied guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print can be isolated. The stock rose about 7% in October around the storm (AAII 2026-10-20).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced through the October rebound. What is not yet visible is any company-quantified October new-business number, which the call can supply.
findings.independence: https://www.mysuncoast.com/2026/10/10/hurricane-isaias-brings-flooding-damage-widespread-power-outages-florida-panhandle/ reports the flooding. Same event, a different outlet.

findings.finding: The NFIP authorization was extended from Sept 30 to Dec 11, 2026 (CRS revision dated 2026-09-11), so there was no Oct 1 lapse this year. Last year's 43-day lapse (from Oct 1, 2025) halted NFIP new and renewal policies and, per management, drove agent adoption of Neptune in Q4 2025. Q4 2026 therefore faces a tougher comp, which caps how far the Q4-implied guide can rise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Feb 2026 print, covering the lapse-boosted Q4 2025 with a first FY guide, moved +12.74%.
findings.why_not_priced: Sell-side Q4 models may still carry last year's lapse-driven new-business run-rate. If the comp were priced, FY consensus would not already sit above the guide.
findings.independence: The 43-day 2025 lapse is documented in https://lereta.com/blog/nfip-deadline-2026-what-servicers-need-to-know/. The adoption benefit is from Q2 coverage (https://www.reinsurancene.ws/neptune-sees-record-figures-in-q226-with-revenue-reaching-55-9m-and-net-income-15-8m/). The Dec 11 date is inferred from a CRS redline, not an enacted-law page.

findings.finding: Capital return: $94.1M remains on the $100M repurchase program as of June 30 (1.22M shares bought in Q2 at $25-26.40). The revolver, however, is $233M drawn of $260M after a $7M July repayment, so further buybacks must come from free cash flow, about $35M of quarterly adj. EBITDA. A Q3 buyback disclosure, or an upsized facility, could be a modest support.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No print has turned on capital return. The May 2026 concurrent buyback came with a secondary sale.
findings.why_not_priced: Small, and dependent on undisclosed Q3 activity. It is in the 10-Q but rarely in previews.
findings.independence: Shares a document with finding 1 (the 10-Q) but a different line. No other source.

outside_window.finding: The NFIP authorization now expires Dec 11, 2026. A lapse then would again halt NFIP new and renewal business and favour private flood carriers, but it resolves after the exit window.
The FEMA Review Council recommends gradually moving NFIP policies to the private market. It needs statutory change, nothing is scheduled inside the window, and the guide excludes it.

baseline_tension: There is no skew or implied move to cut against. The stock's 16% drawdown from its post-Q2 high and the rising short interest look like the market already leaning on the quiet-season demand worry, so the negatives here agree with the tape and are partly priced, while the guide-conservatism positive cuts against it.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (narrow proxy, macro transmission): the hurricane-salience finding went from -1.5 to -1.2 and the housing finding from -0.5 to -0.4; both stay filed as proxies with independence saying so.

Rule 6 (verify the bar): the bar is sourced to the company guide plus Zacks/EW/TickFlow, which roughly agree, so nothing is capped. I note that the Street FY is already above the $199M guide, so a token raise is not a beat.
Rule 1 (reaction history): beat-and-raise prints were bought (+12.7%, about +6.7% gap) and a small beat was sold (-3.2%), so the guide finding keeps +1.5 and p_up stays at 55 rather than higher.
Rule 7 (positioning before negatives): short interest checked, 2.46M shares and 3.8 days to cover, not crowded, so the negatives are not shrunk for squeeze risk.
